$$

Multiplying a matrix by the corresponding identity matrix leaves every entry unchanged. Both matrices are $3\times3$, so the product is defined.

$$
AI_3=A=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 8 & 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ is the third row of $I_3$. Multiplying $B$ on the left by this row selects the third row of $B$. Therefore,

$$
AB=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{5} & 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Notice that $B$ is the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}.$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ by the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3},$ the result must be the $2$nd *column* of $A.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot 0+\left(\frac{-\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\cdot 1+0\cdot 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot 0+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot 1+0\cdot 0 \\ 0\cdot 0+0\cdot 1+1\cdot 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
